key_insight: Instead of only adding more computation steps, Latent Lattice Language Models increase the number of internal states active at once. They combine latent streams that carry information across time with a residual stream that carries information through model depth.
problem_solved: Conventional approaches scale per-token computation through deeper layers, repeated layers, or latent reasoning steps. This paper explores a complementary direction: expanding the model's active computational state.
method: Introduce a “Lattice of Latents”: per-layer horizontal latent streams that recur across time.
Maintain a vertical residual stream that passes information through model depth.
Combine these time- and depth-directed streams to expand internal computational capacity.
impact: The architecture offers practitioners an alternative dimension for scaling language models beyond depth or repeated computation. The provided abstract is incomplete, so performance gains and efficiency trade-offs cannot be assessed.
visual_elements: A lattice diagram with time on the horizontal axis and model depth on the vertical axis.
Color-coded arrows distinguishing recurrent latent streams from the vertical residual stream.
A side-by-side comparison of a conventional residual-stack model and the proposed latent lattice.
A scaling illustration contrasting more computation steps with more active internal states.
paper_authors: Shivam Duggal, Zongze Wu, William T. Freeman, Antonio Torralba, Richard Zhang
